reference: There is no matching GNU man(1) CLI oracle for this minimal Bash builtin. Expected results are contract values from loadables/man.c's public help/source documentation plus fixed roff inputs rendered independently according to its documented supported subset. Bash type/help availability is checked through Bash's own metadata builtins. No expectation is copied from candidate output.
coverage: Bash builtin type and help metadata availability.
Roff from stdin: section headings, paragraph spacing, comments, font escapes and common special characters.
No-fill blocks preserve literal indentation and spacing.
Relative -f file rendering and file-not-found diagnostics.
Relative MANPATH lookup, explicit section selection, -w path output and colon-list search order.
Missing page and incomplete option diagnostics.
exclusions: Full man-db/mandoc formatting and advanced roff requests such as tables, pic and eqn are outside this minimal renderer contract.
The interactive /bash-os/man.sh pager wrapper and installed system man-page corpus are not exercised; cases use stdin or private relative fixtures only.

cases.purpose: The target is advertised to Bash as a builtin and has help metadata. This checks Bash type/help behavior without invoking man-page lookup.
cases.script:
type -t man
help man > metadata-output
printf 'help entry available\n'

cases.purpose: The documented man - interface renders a bounded roff stream. The literal expected text is independently transcribed from the documented SH/SS, PP, comment, font and common-special subset.
cases.script:
man - <<'ROFF'
.TH DEMO 1
.\" ignored comment
.SH NAME
demo \- sample \(co
.PP
A \fBbold\fR and \fIitalic\fR word.
.SS NOTES
literal \\ path and \&sign.
ROFF
cases.stdout:
NAME
demo - sample (c)

A bold and italic word.

  NOTES
literal \ path and sign.

cases.purpose: The documented minimal roff renderer supports .nf/.fi; this fixed input checks that a no-fill block keeps leading and repeated spaces while surrounding paragraph structure is rendered.
cases.script:
man - <<'ROFF'
.TH BLOCK 1
.SH EXAMPLE
.nf
  first  line
    second line
.fi
.PP
after
ROFF
cases.stdout:
EXAMPLE
  first  line
    second line

after

cases.purpose: The documented -f PATH form reads a relative page file and renders its section, body, paragraph break and alternating bold request. The expected text is hand-derived from the literal fixture.
cases.script:
printf '%s\n' '.TH LOCAL 1' '.SH NAME' 'local \- file page' '.PP' '.BR bold (1)' > local.1
man -f local.1

cases.purpose: Private pages in sections 1 and 3 exercise the documented MANPATH search, -w resolved-path output, explicit -s selection and SECTION NAME shorthand. The path and rendered strings are fixed by the relative fixture.
cases.script:
mkdir -p manuals/man1 manuals/man3
printf '%s\n' '.TH SAMPLE 1' '.SH SECTION' 'one' > manuals/man1/sample.1
printf '%s\n' '.TH SAMPLE 3' '.SH SECTION' 'three' > manuals/man3/sample.3
MANPATH=manuals man -w sample
MANPATH=manuals man -s 3 sample
MANPATH=manuals man 1 sample

cases.purpose: The documented colon-separated MANPATH lookup uses the first root that contains the requested page. Two private roots make the selected relative path and rendered page unambiguous.
cases.script:
mkdir -p first/man1 second/man1
printf '%s\n' '.SH SOURCE' 'first-root' > first/man1/choose.1
printf '%s\n' '.SH SOURCE' 'second-root' > second/man1/choose.1
MANPATH=first:second man -w choose
MANPATH=first:second man choose

cases.purpose: A name absent from the private MANPATH produces no page text, a failing status and a diagnostic; wording is intentionally not pinned because the documented contract only requires lookup/render behavior.
The documented -f PATH form reports a missing relative fixture file as an error without rendering output.
The documented -s SECTION form requires its section argument; an incomplete invocation returns a usage failure and emits a diagnostic without page output.
After empty stdin reaches EOF, the next invocation must read its newly redirected stream and ignore the unknown request; exact body output must remain visible.
cases.script: : > empty; man - < empty; printf '.UNKNOWN ignored\nplain\n' | man -

cases.purpose: A fresh stdin invocation ignores an unsupported roff request and emits its following body.
Each man invocation must consume its current private stdin after prior empty and nonempty files reached EOF; unknown requests are ignored and render state resets between sources.
cases.script:
: > empty
printf '.SH FIRST\nfirst-body\n' > first
printf '.UNKNOWN ignored\nsecond-body\n' > second
for page in empty first empty second; do
 man - < "$page"
done
